title: Enforce NIP-34 status authority before mutating Gitea issue state
description: reflectIssueStatus (internal/reflector/reflector.go:225-269) maps root->issue but never checks the status author is owner/maintainer/issue-author. With NIP34_STATUS_SYNC_ENABLED any signed kind 1630-1633 referencing a reflected issue can close/reopen it. Fix: define and enforce the status authority model (owner/maintainer, and original author where appropriate) before SetIssueState.
acceptance_criteria: Status events from unauthorized authors do not change issue state; authorized authors still work; test covers unauthorized close attempt
close_reason: Closed

title: Gate Hive-CI execution to owner-authored workflows only
description: Any patch/PR event mapped to a repo executes workflow files via act with no repo allowlist, approval gate, timeout, resource/concurrency limit, or sandbox (internal/hiveci/runner.go:120-235,376-430). A contributor PR workflow = arbitrary code execution (host compromise if act has Docker socket). Per user: CI is expected to run ONLY owner-authored workflows. Fix: verify the workflow/commit is authored by the repo owner/maintainer before running; add per-run timeout and concurrency limits; document isolation expectations. (Full untrusted-contributor sandboxing is out of scope for now.)
acceptance_criteria: Workflows from non-owner/non-maintainer authors are not executed; per-run timeout + concurrency cap enforced
close_reason: Closed

title: Restrict outbound fetches of Nostr-supplied URLs (SSRF)
description: Attacker-controlled kind-0 'picture' URLs (gitea/profile.go:111-162 downloadImage) and event 'clone' URLs (reflector.go:331-395, proactivesync/service.go:296-357) are fetched / git-fetched with http.DefaultClient following redirects, no scheme/private-IP/loopback/metadata restriction. SSRF to internal services + cloud metadata; avatar bytes create an exfil channel. Fix: HTTPS-only, per-redirect resolved-address validation, deny private/loopback/link-local ranges and file/helper protocols, allowlist git clone sources, preferably egress proxy.
acceptance_criteria: Fetches to private/loopback/link-local/metadata addresses are blocked including via redirect; non-HTTPS rejected; clone sources validated
close_reason: Closed

title: Prevent NIP-05 local-part collisions capturing existing orgs/users/repos
description: Org/repo names use only the sanitized NIP-05 local part; domain is discarded (internal/nip05resolve/resolve.go:126-187, provisioner.go:195-265), so admin@attacker.example and admin@legit.example both map to 'admin'. EnsureOrg/EnsureRepo (gitea/client.go:56-116) silently adopt existing Gitea objects; ResolveOrCreate (auth/identity.go:104-153) binds an attacker pubkey to an existing username on CreateUser failure. No uniqueness constraint on gitea_user_id. Enables tenant/account takeover. Fix: domain-qualified collision-resistant naming, reserve existing tenants, require explicit ownership-link ceremony before binding existing Gitea user/org, add uniqueness constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Two distinct NIP-05 domains with same local part map to distinct Gitea namespaces; existing org/user is never silently adopted; DB uniqueness constraint on gitea identity
close_reason: Closed

title: Fail closed when ADMIN_API_TOKEN is unset (remove open mode)
description: requireAuth (internal/api/server.go:120-125) allows ALL requests when apiToken is empty. /provision, /signer/authorize, /mappings, /outbound-events, /metrics use requireAuth (not the fail-closed requireConfiguredAuth). A missing/misspelled token exposes tenant creation and persistent signer-grant ops to the internet. User has confirmed open mode is NOT deliberate. Fix: fail startup in production without ADMIN_API_TOKEN (config.go Load validation), and route every mutation/signer/queue/mapping/metrics endpoint through fail-closed auth.
acceptance_criteria: Startup errors in production if ADMIN_API_TOKEN unset; all sensitive endpoints reject unauthenticated requests; no open-mode fallthrough remains
close_reason: Closed

title: Authorize inbound repository-state events before mutating refs
description: HandleStateEvent (internal/proactivesync/service.go:100-146 -> applyStateEvent/reconcileDeletedRefs:397-449) validates only event ID+signature, then trusts the unauthenticated 'p' tag to select the repo mapping and applies state locally, including deleting any local branch/tag omitted from the event. Any Nostr key can sign a kind:30618 with p=<victim-owner> d=<victim-repo> and wipe/rewrite refs. Embedded relay accepts all state events unconditionally (embedded_full.go makeEmbeddedRelayRejectPolicy). Fix: resolve owner announcement + recursive maintainer set before ALL live state handling; reject unauthorized state before CI/purgatory/git mutation; treat 'p' as a hint only.
acceptance_criteria: Unauthorized kind:30618 for a repo the author does not own/maintain is rejected before any ref mutation; owner/maintainer set resolved from announcement; regression test covers ref-deletion attack
close_reason: Inbound kind:30618 now resolves validated owner/recursive maintainer authority before ref mutation; spoofed-p deletion regression added.

title: P0: Serve relay + NIP-11 at GRASP root
description: Production runs sidecar mode with embedded relay disabled. Deploy full build or multiplex relay at grasp.sharegap.net/ — WebSocket relay + HTTP NIP-11 negotiation on /. NIP-11 must include supported_grasps=[GRASP-01] and repo_acceptance_criteria; curation only if real curation; do not advertise GRASP-02 until validated. Code: cmd/grasp-bridge/embedded_full.go. [Epic: phase1-0kl / sharegap issue #2]
close_reason: Relay + NIP-11 multiplexed at the public root in the full build; NIP-11 carries supported_grasps=[GRASP-01] + repo_acceptance_criteria (+curation only when allowlisted). Production must deploy the full build per deploy/grasp-canonical.env.example — live check in final gate.

title: P0: Consolidate canonical GRASP hostname (grasp.sharegap.net everywhere)
description: Make grasp.sharegap.net canonical in bridge + deploy config. New 30617 announcements must carry both clone=https://grasp.sharegap.net/<npub>/<id>.git and relays=wss://grasp.sharegap.net. Migrate/republish existing announcements+mappings. Gitea /org/repo.git URLs are not canonical GRASP URLs. [Epic: phase1-0kl / sharegap issue #2]
close_reason: Canonical hostname support implemented in config/provisioner/webhook with tests + deploy example. Announcement republish for existing repos requires owner signatures (NIP-46 grants) — that migration is exercised in final gate phase1-boi.

title: P0: Unauthenticated public GRASP Git Smart HTTP (no Gitea auth leak)
description: internal/api/githttp_npub.go reverse-proxies to Gitea which enforces Basic auth before the pre-receive hook runs. Keep public Smart HTTP unauthenticated; authenticate bridge-to-Gitea internally with a scoped service identity; strip caller Authorization/proxy-auth/cookies; never surface WWW-Authenticate: Basic; inject backend authority only after npub/identifier mapping succeeds; fail closed if the pre-receive hook is missing. Acceptance: git ls-remote without credentials works; mismatching push rejected by hook not 401. [Epic: phase1-0kl / sharegap issue #2]
close_reason: Proxy hardening implemented + tested. Deployment still needs a scoped Gitea service account exposed as GIT_BACKEND_USER/GIT_BACKEND_PASSWORD and private-network restriction of the backend — covered by final gate phase1-boi.

title: GRASP-01 compliance for grasp.sharegap.net (sharegap issue #2)
description: Umbrella epic tracking https://git.sharegap.net/cascadia/grasp-gitea/issues/2 — make grasp.sharegap.net a genuine GRASP-01 service (spec a7d3f8b, ngit-grasp 8950bf6). Core rule: Git Smart HTTP is unauthenticated; push authorization comes from signed Nostr repository-state events, not Gitea credentials. Definition of done: canonical single host, credential-free clone/push, signed-state authorization, grasp-audit passes, real ngit flow succeeds.

title: Full-proxy readiness check instead of trusting GITEA_FULL_PROXY_ENABLED flag
description: Oracle PR 1B review P1: config requires GITEA_FULL_PROXY_ENABLED=true before BRIDGE_TOKENS_ENABLED, but nothing verifies the proxy fallback is actually installed and Gitea is network-isolated. Tokens could be minted in a deployment that cannot enforce their scopes. Add a startup readiness check (probe that unmatched Gitea traffic routes through the bridge; optionally verify Gitea is unreachable from outside the private network) once PR 1C/1D land, or keep token endpoints operationally disabled until then.
notes: Implemented in PR 1D: /ready endpoint (unauthenticated, no-store, ok/error only) checks store Ping + giteaproxy.UpstreamProbe (bounded GET to configured gitea base path + /api/healthz, requires 2xx, drains body). Wired only when FullProxyEnabled; compose healthcheck points at it. NOTE: this proves the bridge can reach Gitea, NOT that nginx actually routes through the bridge or that Gitea is network-isolated. Those remain operator preconditions verified by scripts/fullproxy-cutover-verify.sh and the runbook.
close_reason: Readiness probe implemented and wired (see notes). Remaining routing/isolation assurance is covered by the cutover verification script and runbook preconditions rather than a startup assertion.

title: Validate deployed Gitea PAT/auth assumptions
description: Confirm against the DEPLOYED gitea image (not just source tree): admin-created user PATs via POST /api/v1/users/{username}/tokens with Basic admin:adminPAT; delete-by-id/name; exact PAT scope strings; git smart HTTP accepts PAT as Basic password; docker /v2 challenge realm path + registry token lifetime config; reverse-proxy auth header name in deploy/gitea app.ini; ROOT_URL = bridge public URL. Source-tree validation already done: routers/api/v1/api.go L1078 group gated reqSelfOrAdmin + reqBasicOrRevProxyAuth; services/auth/basic.go accepts PAT as basic password with IsBasicAuth=true; CreateAccessToken requires non-empty normalized scopes and returns plaintext once.
notes: Validation script: scripts/z88-gitea-validate.sh (run from a host reaching Gitea directly; needs GITEA_URL, GITEA_ADMIN_USER, GITEA_ADMIN_PAT, TEST_USER; optional TEST_PRIVATE_REPO, PKG_OWNER, PUBLIC_URL). Automates: Basic-only PAT mint (negative 'token' header check), write:package+write:repository scope acceptance, bogus-scope rejection, delete by id AND name, git smart HTTP Basic+PAT (auth + anonymous-refused), generic package upload/download Basic, nuget index Basic, /v2 challenge realm+service parse, registry token via Basic, JWT exp-iat lifetime (<=600s gate). Manual: app.ini reverse-proxy auth header X-Grasp-Auth-User, ROOT_URL=public origin, external-unreachability check, JWT lifetime setting if over bound. Cleans up its PATs and scratch package.

title: PR 1D: nginx full-proxy cutover + deployment validation
description: All Gitea HTTP traffic routes nginx->bridge->Gitea (gated by GITEA_FULL_PROXY_ENABLED). Keep auth_request session handoff but continuation goes through bridge with X-Grasp-Session-Proxy + X-Grasp-Edge-Secret (constant-time verify); strip header set (X-Grasp-*, X-WEBAUTH-USER, X-Forwarded-User, Proxy-Authorization) at every public location AND again in bridge. proxy_request_buffering off everywhere; proxy_buffering off + ~1h timeouts for git//v2/packages/LFS; remove direct public nginx->Gitea routes; readiness endpoint; rollback template + docs; graceful shutdown ~5min configurable. Run the 12 Phase-1 acceptance tests from the Oracle plan.
notes: PR 1D code+config landed. NOT YET VERIFIED AGAINST A LIVE DEPLOYMENT: docker daemon down and nginx absent in the dev environment, so nginx -t and every e2e acceptance test are unrun. Compensating control: internal/api/nginx_routing_test.go models nginx location selection against the real config file (routing, complete internal-header clearing driven by giteaproxy.InternalHeaders, handoff-only trusted identity, streaming buffering, push limits, legacy rollback). Before closing: run nginx -t, run scripts/fullproxy-cutover-verify.sh, and complete its manual list (large clone/push, pre-receive authority, private-repo flip, browser handoff, package client, external isolation check, log hygiene). Blocked by phase1-z88.

title: PR 1C: internal/giteaproxy streaming reverse proxy + git credential translation
description: New internal/giteaproxy: single shared httputil.ReverseProxy (fixed target from GiteaURL, streaming FlushInterval, no body buffering, no env proxy, connection pooling, no whole-request timeout, upgrade support). Credential precedence: trusted session handoff (edge shared secret) > bridge token Basic (username must equal npub or GiteaUser) > Bearer grasp_v1_ > direct NIP-98 (later phases) > passthrough non-bridge creds on ordinary paths > anonymous. Surface/action classifier (git|packages|container|api|lfs|web x read|write|token_exchange|session). Git smart HTTP: upload-pack=git:read, receive-pack=git:write, inject Basic GiteaUser:PAT. Mapped npub paths: bridge token -> per-user PAT; anonymous -> live Repository.Private check (fail closed, no caching) then service identity; invalid grasp_v1_ cred -> 401 never fallthrough. Refactor gitHTTPNpubProxy to delegate; root / dispatch: WS upgrade or nostr+json -> relay, else gitea fallback. Never retry after body bytes sent; sanitize downstream 401 when injected PAT fails (502 + audit).
close_reason: PR 1C complete: internal/giteaproxy streaming reverse proxy (fixed upstream, no body buffering, per-request plan via context), surface/action classifier, credential precedence with bridge-token translation to hidden PATs, live repository identity+visibility verification for mapped npub paths. Oracle P0s fixed (Gitea 'internal' visibility now denies anonymous access; mapped requests verify HookInstalled + live repo ID so a recreated repo can't bypass grasp-pre-receive) and P1s (no bridge-credential shape falls through to Gitea, canonical Host/X-Forwarded-*, exact-origin redirect rewriting incl. mapped responses, mint/retire lock sharing, edge secret strength). nginx cutover tracked in phase1-3fs.

title: PR 1B: bridge token API (mint/list/revoke/rotate) + replay-safe payload-aware NIP-98
description: Add auth.TokenService + TokenHandler: POST /auth/token, GET /auth/tokens, DELETE /auth/tokens/{id}, POST /auth/tokens/{id}/rotate — all NIP-98 authed with atomic replay claims (INSERT OR IGNORE into nip98_replay_claims). Add VerifyNIP98WithPayload + VerifyAndClaimNIP98 to auth.Service (reuse cascadia-go/nip98, canonical target from BridgePublicURL, never Host header). Reuse IdentityService.ResolveOrCreate; per-user striped locks for PAT ensure; max 50 active tokens/pubkey; 16KiB body cap; TTL default 30d, bounds 1h-90d; rotation = atomic revoke+replace. Explicitly register SessionHandoffHandler in main.go + integration test. Cleanup/audit jobs. Feature-flagged until 1C/1D deployed.
close_reason: PR 1B complete: TokenService (mint/list/revoke/rotate + Authenticate + DownstreamPAT + PAT lifecycle/retirement/reseal), TokenHandler HTTP API, payload-aware NIP-98 with durable replay claims. Oracle review P0s fixed (gitea_token_id migration for PR1A upgrades, identity-link verification w/ quarantine, detached-context PAT rollback + ambiguous-create reconciliation) and P1s (PAT retirement sweep, lazy reseal, SQL-conditional usage throttle, Npub/GiteaUser on principal, Gitea response validation). Full-proxy readiness check filed separately.

title: PR 1A: token/PAT persistence, credential crypto, Gitea PAT admin client
description: Foundation for bridge tokens. Add SQLite tables (bridge_tokens, gitea_pat_credentials, nip98_replay_claims, auth_audit_events) + CRUD in internal/store/auth_tokens.go; AES-256-GCM credential key ring (GRASP_CREDENTIAL_KEYS, separate from SignerMasterKey) in internal/auth/credential_crypto.go; config for TTL bounds/edge secret/full-proxy flag/audit retention/shutdown grace; extend internal/gitea/client.go with CreateUserAccessToken/DeleteUserAccessToken (MUST use Basic auth admin:adminPAT — endpoint gated by reqBasicOrRevProxyAuth, validated against gitea source routers/api/v1/api.go L1078-1083) and Repository.Private decoding. No routing changes; independently compilable.
design: Token: grasp_v1_ + 43ch base64url (32B crypto/rand); store SHA-256 hash BLOB unique. One active hidden PAT per gitea user (generation counter, provisioning|active|retiring|orphaned|error states, create-before-retire rotation). AAD = gitea_user_id, generation, pat_name, key_id. Scopes closed enum: git:read git:write packages:read packages:write api:read api:write lfs:read lfs:write; phase 1 enables git:* only.
close_reason: PR 1A merged (421026d): schema+CRUD for bridge_tokens/gitea_pat_credentials/nip98_replay_claims/auth_audit_events, CredentialCipher key ring, config validation, Gitea PAT admin client via Basic auth. Oracle review findings all addressed. Deployed-image validation tracked separately in phase1-z88 (blocks production enablement, not code).

title: Epic: nostr auth for every Gitea HTTP surface (full-proxy bridge + bridge tokens)
description: Make grasp-gitea a comprehensive nostr interoperability bridge: a nostr identity can auth to EVERY Gitea HTTP surface (private git over smart HTTP, all package registries, REST API, LFS). Chosen architecture (Oracle plan at prompt-exports/oracle-plan-2026-07-30-161341-untitled-chat-852430-c7ad.md): bridge becomes the full reverse proxy for Gitea; bridge-issued opaque tokens (grasp_v1_ prefix, NIP-98-authenticated mint/list/revoke/rotate) verified at the edge and translated to hidden per-user Gitea PATs (encrypted at rest, minted via admin API). Direct NIP-98 on bounded requests later.

title: Loom Phase 2: outbound Hive-CI-over-Loom dispatch (trusted/free workers)
description: Design: docs/designs/loom-integration.md §4,§7,§11 Phase 2. Add worker-ad pool + canonical-latest selection (kind 10100, allowlist-gated); mint ephemeral publisher keypair; NIP-44 encrypt HIVE_CI_NSEC to worker; build+publish kind 5401 workflow-run and kind 5100 job request; persist immutable dispatch attempt + signed event bytes BEFORE publish (idempotent republish). Route outbound author authorization through nostrauthz.Resolver (share with hiveci). Trusted-fleet payment mode (static/absent token); real Cashu deferred to Phase 3. Inbound 5402 verified against ephemeral publisher, 5101/30100 against worker, with full dispatch-field matching + monotonic state machine + ordering.
acceptance_criteria: Authorized push dispatches 5401+5100 to an allowlisted worker; unauthorized author never dispatched; HIVE_CI_NSEC round-trips; inbound 5402/5101 gated by dispatch record and signer; 30100 ordering (created_at desc,id) + future-skew rejection + terminal monotonicity covered by tests.
close_reason: Closed

title: Loom Phase 1: Gitea commit-status writer + reflect Tier-A CI runs
description: Smallest correct slice of Loom integration (design: docs/designs/loom-integration.md §11 Phase 1). Add internal/gitea/status.go CreateCommitStatus (POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/statuses/{sha}); add internal/store/loomjobs.go correlation table (bounded TTL); add internal/loom/ inbound consumer + status mapper via a neutral StatusSink interface; route existing internal/hiveci/runner.go local act results through the sink so CI finally surfaces in the Gitea UI (no Loom submission, no payment). Wire kinds/subscriber/config/main.go. Status delivery must be independently retryable and never re-run work on POST failure.
acceptance_criteria: Local Tier-A act runs produce Gitea commit statuses (pending->terminal) on the dispatch-record SHA; runner decoupled from gitea.Client via StatusSink; correlation store bounded; tests for commit-status POST, TTL, terminal-state mapping.
notes: Implemented canonical Loom Phase 1 only. Added durable Gitea status outbox, bounded immutable correlation, inbound 30100/5101/5402 validation/order/precedence, and Tier-A status reflection with an atomic execution claim. Canonical mode suppresses legacy 25910 dispatch; outbound 5401/5100, worker selection, payment, and log fetching remain deferred to existing Phase 2/3 work.
close_reason: Acceptance met: Tier-A pending-to-terminal statuses on dispatch SHA, neutral StatusSink, bounded TTL store, canonical inbound hardening, and required tests/gates green.

title: Gate state CI with proactive authorization
description: Item D-owned cmd/grasp-bridge/main.go currently calls publisherSvc.HandleStateEventCI before proactiveSyncSvc.HandleStateEvent. Call proactiveSyncSvc.AuthorizeStateEvent first and skip CI/sync on authorization error so unauthorized kind:30618 is rejected before CI. Hook added by Item A; see security remediation plan cross-item note.
close_reason: Closed

title: Update admin API tests for fail-closed empty token
description: internal/api/server_test.go still asserts legacy open-mode behavior when ADMIN_API_TOKEN is empty. Update TestNoAuthRequiredWhenTokenEmpty and TestProvisionBodySizeLimit setup/expectations to require fail-closed 503 or configure a bearer token. Source change is complete under phase1-7fr; test file was outside Item D ownership.
close_reason: Closed

title: Require master key for production durable signing + pass merged relay set
description: A production Signet signer is allowed without SIGNER_MASTER_KEY; the durable client key is then persisted with a plaintext marker (signer/server_session.go:181-215, main.go:64-88). The production check (config.go:142-171) only rejects BRIDGE_NSEC, not unencrypted NIP-46 session storage. Also newServerSigner receives cfg.RelayURLs rather than the merged embedded relay list, so embedded-only deployments can't supply fallback relays to a bunker URI lacking relay params. Fix: require a master key for production durable signing; pass the effective merged relay set to signer construction.
acceptance_criteria: Production durable signing requires SIGNER_MASTER_KEY (no plaintext session storage); signer receives merged embedded+configured relay set
close_reason: Closed

title: Implement Loom integration (currently absent)
description: Pillar 5 (Loom/Hive-CI): Hive-CI has a partial runner but Loom integration is entirely absent from grasp-gitea. This is a greenfield feature requiring a design pass first: define how Loom protocol events map to Gitea CI/status, subscription kinds, publication path, and config. See loom-protocol/ and hive-ci-protocol/ roots for the specs. Fix: produce a design doc under docs/designs then implement. Blocks pillar-5 completeness.
design: Design pass complete: docs/designs/loom-integration.md. grasp-gitea = Hive-CI orchestrator/Loom client targeting canonical Loom+Hive kinds (5100/5101/30100/5102/5401/5402), NOT the cascadia 25910 dialect. Inbound results -> Gitea commit status via new CreateCommitStatus, anchored in an immutable dispatch-record correlation store; outbound author authz via nostrauthz; Cashu payment phased. Implementation split into child beads phase1-asj (P1 status writer+Tier-A reflect), phase1-5de (P2 outbound dispatch), phase1-zrk (P3 Cashu+Blossom+cancel), phase1-pwy (P4 dialect reconcile, gated on maintainer Q1). Open questions for maintainer in doc §12.
acceptance_criteria: Loom protocol events consumed/published per spec; design doc recorded; wired into bridge composition root
notes: Design linked: docs/designs/loom-integration.md. Reviewed by Oracle (review mode); hardening folded in: 30100 replaceable ordering scoped to worker author + created_at/id tie-break + future-skew, monotonic terminal state machine, dispatch-durability-before-publish, dedicated LOOM_RELAY_URLS subscriber (embedded relay rejects unknown kinds), commit-availability awaiting_git_object retry, worker-trust caveat (worker holds HIVE_CI_NSEC), webhook-vs-relay authz distinction. Bead kept open to track implementation phases.
close_reason: Canonical Loom/Hive-CI integration delivered across Phase 1 (phase1-asj: commit-status writer + Tier-A reflect), Phase 2 (phase1-5de: outbound worker dispatch, NIP-44 key handoff, durable idempotent publish), and Phase 3 (phase1-zrk: Cashu payment, Blossom log ingestion, 5102 cancellation). Design: docs/designs/loom-integration.md. Phase 4 (cascadia dialect) closed as moot. Remaining follow-up: phase1-36y (upstream Go 1.26 race crash).

title: Make webhook delivery durable before acknowledging (no silent loss)
description: All publication errors return HTTP 200 to prevent Gitea retries (webhook/handler.go:117-177). Actor-authored events use the durable outbox, but bridge-signed status/CI/fallback paths and failures before enqueue are lost permanently. Fix: persist webhook delivery IDs and processing state before acknowledging, then retry internally; return 200 only after durable acceptance.
acceptance_criteria: Webhook deliveries are durably recorded before 200; failed bridge-signed paths retried, not lost
close_reason: Closed

title: Advance repository state tracking after owner-signed outbox publication
description: Bridge-signed publication calls RecordStatePublished, but the owner-signed outbox path (publisher/service.go:230-298,339-369; outbox/worker.go:220-266) only marks the queue row published, leaving mappings.last_state_digest stale so every mirror callback re-enqueues the same state relying on dedupe-key collisions. Fix: carry mapping/digest publication metadata with the outbox row and atomically update repository publication state after successful relay publication.
acceptance_criteria: last_state_digest updates after owner-signed publication; no repeated re-enqueue of identical state
close_reason: Owner-signed outbox publication now records canonical state digest/event metadata before marking the queue row published.

title: Centralize replaceable-event ordering (created_at + id tie-break)
description: User GRASP-list cache replaces only on greater created_at ignoring NIP-01 equal-timestamp event-id tie-break (store/sqlite.go:1012-1038). Announcement caching overwrites without any replaceable ordering check (provisioner.go:95-174,280-297). Proposed purgatory state is selected by acceptance time not event created_at (store/purgatory.go:92-113). Permits stale-event replay. Fix: centralize canonical replaceable ordering used transactionally for announcements, GRASP lists, and proposed state.
acceptance_criteria: Replaceable ordering (created_at desc, id asc tie-break) enforced consistently for announcements/grasp-lists/proposed state
close_reason: Centralized created_at-desc/event-id-asc ordering for announcements, GRASP lists, and proposed state with strict additive migration

title: Add timeout + resource cleanup to pre-receive relay checks
description: Ordinary state lookup uses context.Background() with no deadline (cmd/grasp-pre-receive/main.go:43-63); FetchLatestRepositoryStateForRepo (nostrstate/state.go:12-66) also never closes the relay connection. A slow/malicious relay stalls Gitea receive workers indefinitely and leaks connections. Fix: short end-to-end timeout and always close relay/subscription resources.
acceptance_criteria: Pre-receive relay lookups have a bounded timeout and close all connections
close_reason: Added one end-to-end hook timeout with derived relay/HTTP/Git contexts and guaranteed relay close

title: Add quotas/limits to public refs/nostr pushes (storage exhaustion)
description: cmd/grasp-pre-receive/main.go:180-224 accepts any valid 64-hex id when no corresponding relay event exists; an anonymous caller can continuously push large unique objects under new IDs. The reaper (refsnostr/reaper.go:92-145) eventually deletes refs but uploaded unreachable objects remain until GC, and nginx permits 1GiB requests. Fix: per-repo/IP quotas, pack/object limits, concurrent-push limits, aggressive unreachable-object maintenance, preferably require proof tying pushed id/tip to a signed event.
acceptance_criteria: Unauthenticated refs/nostr pushes are quota-limited; unreachable objects cleaned promptly
close_reason: Added nginx IP/repo request quotas plus hook ref/pack/object limits and bounded unreachable-object cleanup

title: Persist NIP-34 thread roots and reflect standard NIP-22 comments
description: Issue/PR root references live only in an in-memory threads map (webhook/handler.go:88-100,560-597), so after restart status/PR-update/comment reflection is skipped despite SQLite mappings. Outbound NIP-22 comments omit an 'a' tag while inbound reflector mapping (reflector.go:143-161) requires 'a', so a standards-shaped comment referencing only its root can't reach reflectComment. Fix: persist/query thread roots by Gitea repo/object; resolve comment repo via persisted root event instead of requiring nonstandard 'a' tag.
acceptance_criteria: Thread resolution survives restart; standard NIP-22 comment with only root ref reflects correctly
close_reason: Closed

title: Implement inbound NIP-32 labels and label removal semantics
description: Kind 1985 is neither subscribed (relay/subscriber.go:25-42) nor handled by the reflector (reflector.go:103-141). Gitea 'labeled' and 'unlabeled' both publish the same positive label event (webhook/handler.go:336-343,698-721), so removal has no distinct representation. Fix: implement inbound NIP-32 label mapping + explicit removal/replacement model; add kind 1985 to subscription only once authorization and echo handling exist.
acceptance_criteria: Inbound label events map to Gitea labels; unlabeled produces a distinct removal representation
close_reason: Closed

title: Verify kind-0 event id/signature/author before use
description: nip05resolve/resolve.go:91-160 and nostrprofile/profile.go:49-103 trust events returned under an Authors filter without CheckID/VerifySignature. A malicious relay can forge victim metadata influencing org naming or supplying SSRF avatar URLs. Fix: validate event ID/signature and author before parsing any kind-0 metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Kind-0 events failing id/sig/author checks are rejected before parsing
close_reason: Closed

title: Rate-limit + bound + clean up public NIP-46 init sessions
description: Every unauthenticated NIP-46 init creates a DB row and goroutine (auth/nip46handler.go:103-164,227-285). Bunker setup uses context.WithoutCancel (signer/service.go:209-235, server_session.go:151-177) so the connector goroutine outlives the 30s caller timeout indefinitely. No rate limit/concurrency bound; expired sessions/challenges never cleaned. title: Migrate grasp-gitea from nbd-wtf/go-nostr to fiatjaf.com/nostr
description: The nbd-wtf/go-nostr package is deprecated. Replace all usages with fiatjaf.com/nostr (already a dependency in go.mod). This is a deep API migration: keys/IDs/sigs/kinds move from hex strings to typed [32]byte/[64]byte/uint16; GetPublicKey no longer returns error; RelayConnect requires RelayOptions; event.Sign takes [32]byte; Filter fields are typed; nip19/nip34/nip46/nip05 signatures changed. Drop the old dependency via go mod tidy when complete.
design:
API mapping nbd-wtf/go-nostr v0.52 -> fiatjaf.com/nostr:
TYPES (hex string -> typed): Event.ID string->nostr.ID[32]byte; Event.PubKey string->nostr.PubKey[32]byte; Event.Sig string->[64]byte; Event.Kind int->nostr.Kind(uint16). Convert at store/Gitea/log boundaries via .Hex() and PubKeyFromHex/IDFromHex.
KEYS: GeneratePrivateKey()string -> Generate()SecretKey; GetPublicKey(hex)(string,err) -> GetPublicKey([32]byte)PubKey (no err); IsValidPublicKey(hex) -> use PubKeyFromHex err; nip19.Decode nsec returns [32]byte not string; nip19 Encode* take typed args.
SIGN/VERIFY: event.Sign(hexkey) -> Sign([32]byte); event.CheckSignature()(bool,err) -> VerifySignature()bool; CheckID()bool unchanged.
FILTER: Kinds []int->[]Kind; Authors []string->[]PubKey; IDs []string->[]ID.
RELAY (redesigned): RelayConnect(ctx,url) -> RelayConnect(ctx,url,RelayOptions{}); QuerySync REMOVED -> use QueryEvents(filter) iter.Seq[Event] or pool; Subscribe(ctx,[]Filter) -> Subscribe(ctx,Filter,SubscriptionOptions{}); sub.Events chan; EndOfStoredEvents handling changed; Publish(ctx,Event) value.
NIP34: repo.Maintainers []string -> []nostr.PubKey; Parse* take nostr.Event value.
NIP46: signatures typed. Existing server_signer.go already bridges both pkgs via JSON.
PLAN: (1) flip internal event type wholesale; (2) fix boundary conversions at store layer; (3) rework relay subscribe/query call sites; (4) migrate 25 src files then 21 tests; (5) go build+test green; (6) go mod tidy to drop nbd-wtf.
notes: COMPLETE (on branch migrate-fiatjaf-nostr). All grasp-gitea code + tests migrated nbd-wtf/go-nostr -> fiatjaf.com/nostr. Also migrated khatru+eventstore (used by embedded relay + integration test relay) to fiatjaf.com/nostr/khatru + fiatjaf.com/nostr/eventstore because khatru's API redesigned (single-func handlers, UseEventstore, iterator queries). nbd-wtf fully removed from go.mod/go.sum via go mod tidy. Verified: go build/vet/test ./... AND -tags full all pass (exit 0). Key boundary decision: used PubKeyFromHexCheap (decode-only) for stored-pubkey conversions in webhook to preserve original non-curve-validating behavior. NOT yet committed/pushed.
close_reason: Migrated grasp-gitea from nbd-wtf/go-nostr to fiatjaf.com/nostr; nbd-wtf removed from go.mod/go.sum; default + -tags full build/vet/test all pass

description: internal/webhook (handler.go 403 LOC, types.go 141 LOC) is a live HTTP handler wired at /webhook/gitea in cmd/grasp-bridge/main.go, yet has NO test files (go test reports 'no test files'). It handles HMAC verification, JSON payload parsing for 6 event types (push/create/delete/pull_request/issues/label), and maps them to signed NIP-34 Nostr events. Zero tests means the npub/hex tag bug (see sibling issue) shipped undetected, and any regression in payload parsing or event mapping is invisible. Scope: add handler_test.go covering (1) HMAC accept/reject, (2) method-not-allowed, (3) push -> RepublishForGiteaRepo delegation + CI push hook, (4) pull_request opened/closed -> correct kinds & hex tags, (5) issues opened/closed & labeled -> kinds 1621/1985 with valid hex 'p' and '30617:hex:repo' 'a' tags, (6) unknown-repo webhook is a silent no-op. Use a fake publisher/relay to assert the exact events produced.
acceptance_criteria: webhook package has tests; go test ./internal/webhook passes; tests assert hex pubkeys and valid a-tag coordinates in emitted events
close_reason: Added internal/webhook/handler_test.go: 8 tests covering HMAC accept/reject, method-not-allowed, push delegation+CI hook, unknown-repo no-op, PR opened/merged, issue opened/labeled, and hex-tag regression guards. Introduced Publisher interface for testability.

title: Webhook NIP-34 events use bech32 npub instead of hex pubkey in p/a tags
description: internal/webhook/handler.go builds NIP-34 events (kind 1618/1619/1621/1630-1633/1985) using mapping.Npub (bech32) for 'p' tags and for the repo 'a'-tag coordinate (repoTag = npub/RepoID). Nostr 'p' tags MUST be 32-byte hex pubkeys, and NIP-34 addressable coordinates must be '30617:<hex-pubkey>:<repo-id>'. Consequences: (1) every PR/issue/label/status event is non-compliant and invisible to clients filtering #p by hex; (2) the 'a' coordinate 'npub.../repo' is entirely malformed and cannot be resolved to the repo announcement. The publisher (buildStateEvent, buildWorkflowRunEvent in ci.go) correctly uses mapping.Pubkey (hex), proving the intended pattern. Fix: use mapping.Pubkey for all p tags and build a-tags as fmt.Sprintf('%d:%s:%s', 30617, mapping.Pubkey, mapping.RepoID). Evidence: handler.go lines ~186-300 (repoTag, prRef, {p, mapping.Npub}).
close_reason: Fixed: webhook handler now uses mapping.Pubkey (hex) for all 'p' tags and builds 'a' coordinates as 30617:<hex>:<repo-id> via new repoAddr() helper. Covered by new regression tests (TestNoNpubInSemanticTags, TestPR/Issue_*).

title: Harden reflector echo-loop guard against dropped/duplicate Gitea webhooks
description: The echo guard (reflected_events.echo_pending one-shot, ConsumeReflectedGiteaEcho) is fragile: (1) DROPPED webhook — if the Gitea webhook resulting from a reflection never fires, echo_pending stays 1 forever, so a genuine LATER Gitea change matching (repo,index,kind) is wrongly suppressed; (2) DUPLICATE webhook — Gitea retries deliver the same webhook twice; the first consumes echo_pending=0, so the duplicate is NOT suppressed and leaks an echo to Nostr. Fix: replace the one-shot flag with a time-windowed, content-fingerprinted, NON-consuming guard: on reflection record echo_armed_at + echo_fingerprint (hash of the content the bridge wrote — issue title/body, comment body, state, PR head tip); ConsumeReflectedGiteaEcho suppresses any matching webhook within a short TTL window (default ~5m) AND matching fingerprint (so duplicates within the window are all suppressed and unrelated same-(repo,index,kind) user edits with different content are published); guards past the TTL are treated expired (disarmed lazily/periodically) so a dropped webhook never blocks genuine later events.
acceptance_criteria: duplicate delivery of a reflected webhook is suppressed every time within the window; a dropped webhook expires so a genuine later same-object change is published; a genuine user edit with different content within the window is NOT suppressed (fingerprint mismatch); expired guards are cleaned up; tests cover duplicate, dropped/expired, and fingerprint-mismatch cases
close_reason: Echo guard hardened: internal/echofp per-kind fingerprints; reflected_events.echo_armed_at+echo_fingerprint; CheckReflectedGiteaEcho is windowed (5m), fingerprint-matched, NON-consuming (duplicate-safe) with lazy DisarmExpiredEchoGuards (dropped-safe); webhook+reflector compute matching fingerprints. Tests cover duplicate/dropped/mismatch/expiry. Gate green.

title: handlePatchPush is a stub — refs/nostr patch pushes never emit kind:1631 applied status
description: internal/webhook/handler.go handlePatchPush() (lines ~336-346) contains 'For now, just log — full implementation would fetch from relay' and returns nil without doing work. When a client pushes to refs/nostr/<event-id> (ngit patch workflow), the bridge should (a) fetch the pre-published kind:1617 patch event from the configured relays (or synthesize a minimal one from push metadata) and (b) emit a kind:1631 (applied) status event referencing that patch and the repo. Currently nothing is published, so patch-application state is never reflected on Nostr. This is the concrete remaining work behind epic-publish-001/publish-003. Depends on the hex-pubkey tag fix so synthesized events are compliant.
notes: Unblocked: the hex-pubkey tag fix (phase1-9gl) landed, so synthesized patch events will now be NIP-34 compliant. Remaining work: fetch/synthesize kind:1617 and emit kind:1631 in handlePatchPush (currently still a log-only stub).
close_reason: Implemented: handlePatchPush now (1) validates the refs/nostr/<id> is a 64-hex event id, (2) best-effort fetches the referenced kind:1617 patch via new publisher.FetchEvent (relay QuerySync), and (3) publishes a kind:1631 applied status with e=<patch-id>, a=30617:<hex>:<repo>, p=maintainer(+patch author when resolved), and applied-as-commits=<pushed SHA>. Emission is resilient to fetch failure/propagation lag since the git ref push is authoritative. Note: the bridge intentionally does NOT synthesize+sign a kind:1617 when absent — that would misattribute contributor authorship to the bridge key; the applied-status carries the landed commit instead. Tests: 4 webhook patch-push tests + publisher FetchEvent no-relay test.

title: Epic: NIP-05 domains as an optional organizational unit

title: nostr_identity_links.nip05 stores the derived Gitea namespace, not the NIP-05 identifier
description:
internal/auth/identity.go ResolveOrCreate sets nip05Addr = orgResolver.ResolveOrgName(...), which returns the derived Gitea namespace (e.g. 'alice-example-c-a1b2c3...'), NOT the NIP-05 identifier ('alice@example.com'). That value is persisted in the nostr_identity_links.nip05 column and exposed as ResolvedIdentity.NIP05 (JSON field "nip05"), so any consumer reading it gets a Gitea org name rather than a NIP-05 address. Contrast nostrprofile.Profile.NIP05, which correctly holds the identifier.

Also: the guard 'if resolved == username && !isHexPrefix(resolved)' is effectively just '!isHexPrefix(resolved)', because resolveUsername returns the same cached ResolveOrgName result.

Fix options: (a) have the resolver also return the verified identifier and store that, or (b) rename the column/field to gitea_namespace to match reality. Option (a) is more useful (enables displaying the verified handle and future NIP-05 serving) but requires a migration/backfill for existing rows.

title: Cache + rebroadcast owner-signed kind:10317 user GRASP lists (verbatim)
description: Follow-up from publish-006.
